credential.label: Vercel access token
credential.description: Access token from Vercel Account Settings → Tokens. Choose the personal account or team scope this deployment needs and set an expiration date. The connector never sends it anywhere except api.vercel.com or the configured baseUrl proxy.

guide.content:
# Vercel usage

Vercel REST access token is already configured. Account purpose: Production web applications

Routing defaults to team team_default. This is not a restriction or tenant pin: an explicit teamId or slug overrides it, and teamId: null selects personal scope. The token's Vercel permissions enforce access.

## Projects, deployments and domains

Resolve a team by slug, a project by name, and deployments by the observed
project id. Team ids start with `team_`, project ids with `prj_`, and deployment
ids with `dpl_`. A deployment hostname and a deployment id identify the same
deployment; an alias can later point to a different deployment.

Some project paths accept a project name, but a deployment list's projectId
filter requires the observed `prj_` id. Resolve the name before listing its
deployments; an empty result for a guessed name does not prove absence.
Complete each identifier lookup before starting the reads that depend on it.

The configured team is a routing default, not a restriction. Explicit teamId
or slug selects another team the token can reach; teamId: null selects personal
scope. Vercel token permissions determine access. Prefer an explicit team when
joining resources across several calls.

Read deployment state before its build events. Runtime logs diagnose requests
after a deployment built; build logs explain a failed build. Narrow time windows
before raising collection limits. Generic reads refuse live follow streams;
use the bounded build/runtime readers. Deployment timestamps are milliseconds.

Project domains and deployment aliases are different joins: a project domain
belongs to the project, while an alias identifies its assigned deployment.
Read a pending domain's verification instructions before changing DNS.

## Environment changes

Resolve environment-variable ids using metadata, including target, branch and
custom environment. A key can have distinct production and preview values.
Existing values cannot be retrieved. Supply new values only when the task asks
for a change; confirm the returned id and metadata.

Environment changes apply to future deployments. A new deployment is a separate
write. Promoting an existing deployment does not rebuild it or update embedded
environment values. After an uncertain update, reconcile observable metadata
such as id, targets and comment; reading metadata cannot verify a secret value.

## Explicit files and credentials

Deployment files can reference previously uploaded digests. File uploads accept
explicit bytes and never read a path on the agent's machine. Decrypted-value,
credential-minting, protection-bypass-link, signing and domain move-out operations
are refused; use Vercel's dashboard for those workflows.

## Conventions

- **Paging:** every tool whose output declares `page` is paged: `list_project_env_vars`, `list_teams`, `vercel_api_details`, `vercel_api_read`, `vercel_api_search`. While `page.hasMore` is true, pass `page.nextCursor` back unchanged using the continuation argument its schema declares; keep the original arguments. The last page has no `nextCursor`. At execute_code's per-program call limit, return page.nextCursor and continue in the next program; don't restart.
- **Paging:** a paged `list_*` or `search_*` read takes `limit` (default 20, at most 100) and `cursor`. While `page.hasMore` is true, pass `page.nextCursor` back unchanged as `cursor`; the last page has no `nextCursor`.
- **Results:** `fields` narrows a read's result to the dot paths you name. `truncated` lists the dot paths a result cut for size; the ids that fetch what was cut stay in the result.
- **Hatch:** `vercel_api_search` finds this API's operations and reads no account data, `vercel_api_details` shows one operation's contract, and `vercel_api_read` calls a reviewed read. `vercel_api_write` calls a reviewed write; the host may ask the user to confirm it. An operation without a reviewed verdict is refused. 29 operations are refused by design; use `vercel_api_details` with the method and path to inspect an operation's contract and refusal.
- **Writes:** a write is sent once and never retried. When its outcome is unknown, read the target before repeating it. Writes take no idempotency key.
- **Errors:** codes come from the vendor's statuses and error facts, never its prose. `not_found` means the record does not exist; this API tells absence from a permission gap. It documents no conflict.
- **Withheld values:** a value withheld for safety reads `"[redacted]"`. Writes refuse whole marker values and withheld links; longer prose may mention the marker. Paths and queries refuse any containment.

tools.name: list_teams
tools.description: List the teams this token can reach, with ids/slugs for project joins. A configured team is a routing default, not a restriction.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: list_project_env_vars
tools.description: List a project's environment-variable metadata without decrypting or returning values: keys, types, targets, branches, and custom environments.

teamId.description: Vercel team id. Omit for the connection's default; null for the token owner's personal account.

slug.description: Team slug; overrides the routing default when teamId is omitted.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each metadata item; values cannot be restored.

tools.name: upsert_project_env_var
tools.description: Create or replace one Vercel project environment variable. Changes affect only future deployments; returns metadata without the value.

teamId.description: Vercel team id. Omit for the connection's default; null for the token owner's personal account.

slug.description: Team slug; overrides the routing default when teamId is omitted.

value.description: New value; write input only. Vercel caps a project's environment at 64 KB.

type.description: Storage type. Sensitive values cannot be read back.

targets.description: Default Vercel environments that receive this value.

customEnvironmentIds.description: Custom environment ids that receive this value.

upsert.description: Defaults to true. False refuses to overwrite an existing variable.

tools.name: update_project_env_var
tools.description: Update one Vercel project environment variable by id, sending only the fields that change. Deployments keep their previous values.

teamId.description: Vercel team id. Omit for the connection's default; null for the token owner's personal account.

slug.description: Team slug; overrides the routing default when teamId is omitted.

gitBranch.description: Replacement preview branch, or null to clear it.

tools.name: get_deployment_build_logs
tools.description: Read a deployment's build events and log lines, without following live output. Bounded by limit and 1 MB; filter by build, time, or direction.

teamId.description: Vercel team id. Omit for the connection's default; null for the token owner's personal account.

slug.description: Team slug; overrides the routing default when teamId is omitted.

direction.description: forward (default) reads oldest first; backward reads the newest first.

since.description: Only events at or after this millisecond timestamp.

until.description: Only events at or before this millisecond timestamp.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in the result, e.g. ["events"]. It only narrows the result.

type.description: stdout, stderr, command, exit, deployment-state, and so on.

info.description: Build step, entrypoint, and path when Vercel sends them.

truncated.description: Dot paths cut for size or by the bounded prefix, including events[] and events[].text.

tools.name: get_runtime_logs
tools.description: Collect a deployment's runtime log stream for at most waitMs or limit, then stop. Returns level, message, request path, and status per row.

teamId.description: Vercel team id. Omit for the connection's default; null for the token owner's personal account.

slug.description: Team slug; overrides the routing default when teamId is omitted.

waitMs.description: How long to collect the stream; default 5000.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in the result, e.g. ["logs"]. It only narrows the result.

truncated.description: Dot paths cut for size, including logs[] and logs[].text.

tools.name: vercel_api_upload
tools.description: Upload explicit text or base64 bytes to a Vercel octet-stream operation, such as POST /v2/files for deployment files. Reads no local files.

path.description: Concrete path of an octet-stream operation from vercel_api_search, e.g. /v2/files.

query.description: Query parameters as JSON, named as vercel_api_details lists them.

contentType.description: Content-Type of the bytes; default application/octet-stream.

textBody.description: Raw UTF-8 body. Exclusive with base64Body.

digest.description: SHA-1 of the bytes, sent as x-vercel-digest for /v2/files.

tools.name: vercel_api_search
tools.description: Find Vercel API operations by keyword or path. Returns up to 8 compact matches with the tool that calls each; reads no account data.

query.description: Keywords or a path, e.g. refund charge.

cursor.description: page.nextCursor from the previous search with the same query.

tool.description: The tool that calls it; absent when refused.

named.description: A named tool serving this operation with a projected result; prefer it.

matched.description: The request or response field this operation was found by; call its tool to read the field.

truncated.description: Entry labels cut for size; vercel_api_details on that method and path returns them whole.

tools.name: vercel_api_details
tools.description: Read one Vercel API operation's request contract: path, query and body parameters with types and required names. Reads no account data.

path.description: The path template from search, or a concrete path.

param.description: Return only this parameter, in full.

cursor.description: page.nextCursor from the previous details call with the same method, path and param.

body.description: Body content type and schema. When paged: this page's properties, the required names it delivers or chunks, and the schema's other keywords on the page that carries them.

tool.description: The tool that calls it; absent when refused.

named.description: A named tool serving this operation with a projected result; prefer it.

of.description: The piece this text belongs to, such as parameters.limit.

text.description: Part of that piece's JSON; join the parts in page order, then parse them.

truncated.description: Labels cut for size; their full text arrives as chunks.

page.description: Present when the contract exceeds one answer: pass nextCursor back for the next pieces.

tools.name: vercel_api_read
tools.description: Call a reviewed Vercel API read, including reviewed read-only POST. The operation index checks arguments before anything is sent. Pass page.nextCursor unchanged in the query parameter page.param names. Team selectors override the routing default; token permissions enforce scope.

path.description: Concrete path from search with ids filled in, e.g. /v13/deployments/dpl_123. No query string.

method.description: GET by default; another method only for an operation search routes here.

body.description: Body for a reviewed read-only POST.

query.description: Query parameters as JSON, named as details lists them.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in data, applied to each item of an array, after value safety and privacy filtering.

data.description: Response body after value safety and the connection's privacy filtering.

param.description: Put nextCursor in this vendor parameter, unchanged.

tools.name: vercel_api_write
tools.description: Call a reviewed Vercel API write; method and path are stated for approval, and the operation index checks arguments first. JSON writes only. Use vercel_api_upload for explicit bytes.

path.description: Concrete path from search with ids filled in, e.g. /v13/deployments/dpl_123. No query string.

query.description: Query parameters as JSON, named as details lists them.

body.description: Request body as JSON fields, named as details lists them; form operations are encoded for you.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in data, applied to each item of an array, after value safety and privacy filtering.

data.description: Response body after value safety and the connection's privacy filtering.
